title: Choose the Forge player
question: These first-screen mockups use the documented Forge A Box Squat prescription. Which arrangement should guide the active workout player?

options.label: Session stack
options.thesis: Warm-up, work, and finish remain in one ordered list, with the current movement opened in place.
options.viewport: Forge A and readiness lead into a compact warm-up list. Box Squat opens with 3 × 6, RPE about 6, set rows, previous and planned load, while Help, Pain, and Substitute stay near the docked set action.
options.risk: A long session can require scrolling to review upcoming movements.

options.label: Set table
options.thesis: The whole Box Squat prescription and each set's record sit together like a working field log.
options.viewport: Forge A opens on Box Squat, with 3 × 6 and RPE about 6 above three generous set rows for load and reps. Previous load is shown as a dash when unknown; Help, Pain, and Substitute remain available beside a docked Complete set action.
options.risk: The extra columns may feel dense on a narrow phone, especially while the keyboard is open.

options.label: Current set
options.thesis: One set fills the screen so the next action is unmistakable during training.
options.viewport: A large Set 1 of 3 and 6 reps sit under Box Squat. An editable load and previous-load dash follow, with next-set markers, Quick Help, Pain, Substitute, and a docked Complete set action. Rest becomes an elapsed timer after completion.
options.risk: It hides the full session until the person opens the exercise list.
